name: Question 3
problem:
Which of the following affine transformations are invertible?

- ${T}_{1}:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}5u-2v-5 \\ 10u-4v+1\end{aligned}]$
- ${T}_{2}:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}u-v-4 \\ u+5v+7\end{aligned}]$
- ${T}_{3}:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}2u+4v-2 \\ 3u+6v+3\end{aligned}]$
worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

The transformation is invertible if the matrix $A$ is invertible. That is, if $det(A)\ne 0.$

With this in mind, let's look at each transformation in turn.

- Transformation ${T}_{1}$ is not invertible. Notice that ${T}_{1}$ can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5u-2v-5 \\ 10u-4v+1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5u-2v \\ 10u-4v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}5 & -2 \\ 10 & -4\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the determinant of $A,$ we get

$$
det(A)=|\begin{aligned}5 & -2 \\ 10 & -4\end{aligned}|=-4\cdot 5-(-2)\cdot 10=0.
$$

Since the determinant is zero, ${T}_{1}$ is *not* invertible.

- Transformation ${T}_{2}$ is invertible. Notice that ${T}_{2}$ can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}u-v-4 \\ u+5v+7\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}u-v \\ u+5v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 7\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 5\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 7\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the determinant of $A,$ we get

$$
det(A)=|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 5\end{aligned}|=5\cdot 1-(-1)\cdot 1=6\ne 0.
$$

Since the determinant is nonzero, ${T}_{2}$ is invertible.

- Transformation ${T}_{3}$ is not invertible. Notice that ${T}_{3}$ can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2u+4v-2 \\ 3u+6v+3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2u+4v \\ 3u+6v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ 3 & 6\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the determinant of $A,$ we get

$$
det(A)=|\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ 3 & 6\end{aligned}|=6\cdot 2-4\cdot 3=0.
$$

Since the determinant is zero, ${T}_{3}$ is *not* invertible.

Therefore, the correct answer is "${T}_{2}$ only."

html:
Question 3
?

Which of the following affine transformations are invertible?

  1. T1:[uv]⟶[5u−2v−510u−4v+1]
  2. T2:[uv]⟶[u−v−4u+5v+7]
  3. T3:[uv]⟶[2u+4v−23u+6v+3]
a
T1 only
b
T1 and T2 only
c
T2 only
d
T1 and T3 only
e
T2 and T3 only
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

An affine transformation T:R2→R2 is a function of the form x=Au+b, where x,u, and b are column vectors in R2, and A is a 2×2 matrix.

The transformation is invertible if the matrix A is invertible. That is, if det(A)≠0.

With this in mind, let's look at each transformation in turn.

  • Transformation T1 is not invertible. Notice that T1 can be expressed as [xy]=[5u−2v−510u−4v+1]=[5u−2v10u−4v]+[−51]=[5−210−4]⏟A⋅[uv]⏟u+[−51]⏟b. Computing the determinant of A, we get det(A)=|5−210−4|=−4⋅5−(−2)⋅10=0. Since the determinant is zero, T1 is not invertible.

  • Transformation T2 is invertible. Notice that T2 can be expressed as [xy]=[u−v−4u+5v+7]=[u−vu+5v]+[−47]=[1−115]⏟A⋅[uv]⏟u+[−47]⏟b. Computing the determinant of A, we get det(A)=|1−115|=5⋅1−(−1)⋅1=6≠0. Since the determinant is nonzero, T2 is invertible.

  • Transformation T3 is not invertible. Notice that T3 can be expressed as [xy]=[2u+4v−23u+6v+3]=[2u+4v3u+6v]+[−23]=[2436]⏟A⋅[uv]⏟u+[−23]⏟b. Computing the determinant of A, we get det(A)=|2436|=6⋅2−4⋅3=0. Since the determinant is zero, T3 is not invertible.

Therefore, the correct answer is "T2 only."
